arxiv-2112-14913.title: Lattice QCD calculation of the two-photon exchange contribution to the muonic-hydrogen Lamb shift
arxiv-2112-14913.description: Abstract We develop a method for lattice QCD calculation of the two-photon exchange (TPE) contribution to the muonic-hydrogen Lamb shift. To demonstrate the feasibility of this method, we also present an exploratory study with a gauge ensemble at m π = 142 m_{\pi}=142 MeV.

arxiv-2204-03234.title: Local and 2-local derivations on Lie matrix rings over commutative involutive rings
arxiv-2204-03234.creator: Sh.A. Ayupov 1,2, F. N. Arzikulov 1,3, S. M. Umrzaqov 3
arxiv-2204-03234.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sh.A. Ayupov 1,2, F. N. Arzikulov 1,3, S. M. Umrzaqov 3. In the present paper we prove that every 2-local inner derivation on the Lie ring of skew-adjoint matrices over a commutative ∗ * -ring is an inner derivation. We also apply our technique to various Lie algebras of infinite dimensional skew-adjoint matrix-valued maps on a set, and prove that every 2-local spatial derivation on such algebras is a spatial derivation.

arxiv-2209-02702.title: An IoT-Enriched Event Log for Process Mining in Smart Factories
arxiv-2209-02702.creator: Lukas Malburg, Joscha Grüger, Ralph Bergmann
arxiv-2209-02702.description: Abstract Modern technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT) are becoming increasingly important in various domains, including Business Process Management (BPM) research. One main research area in BPM is process mining, which can be used to analyze event logs, e. g., for checking the conformance of running processes.

arxiv-2306-09275.title: Modified gravity and massive neutrinos: constraints from the full shape analysis of BOSS galaxies and forecasts for Stage IV surveys
arxiv-2306-09275.creator: and Alkistis Pourtsidou
arxiv-2306-09275.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by and Alkistis Pourtsidou. We constrain the growth index γ \gamma by performing a full-shape analysis of the power spectrum multipoles measured from the BOSS DR12 data. We adopt a theoretical model based on the Effective Field theory of the Large Scale Structure (EFTofLSS) and focus on two different cosmologies: γ \gamma CDM and γ ​ ν \gamma\nu CDM, where we also vary the total neutrino mass.

arxiv-2306-13584.title: Revisiting the Optimal PMU Placement Problem in Multi-Machine Power Networks
arxiv-2306-13584.creator: Mohamad H. Kazma, Graduate Student Member, IEEE, Ahmad F. Tah a, Member, IEEE
arxiv-2306-13584.description: Abstract To provide real-time visibility of physics-based states, phasor measurement units (PMUs) are deployed throughout power networks. PMU data enable real-time grid monitoring and control—and are essential in transitioning to smarter grids. Various considerations are taken into account when determining the geographic, optimal PMU placements (OPP). This paper focuses on the control-theoretic, observability aspect of OPP.

arxiv-2312-10836.title: Measuring precise radial velocities on individual spectral lines Thanks: Based on observations made with the HARPS instrument on the ESO 3.6m Telescope at the La Silla Observatory, Chile.
arxiv-2312-10836.creator: K. Al Moulla, X. Dumusque, M. Cretignier
arxiv-2312-10836.description: Abstract Context. Radial velocities (RVs) of stars contain both the Doppler reflex motion of potential planetary companions and the drowning and sometimes imitating effect of stellar activity. To separate the two, previous efforts have sought for proxys which only trace the activity signals, yet the sub-meter-per-second floor required for the detection of Earth-like planets remains difficult to break. Aims.

arxiv-2410-04959.title: Collapse-Proof Non-Contrastive Self-Supervised Learning
arxiv-2410-04959.creator: Emanuele Sansone, Tim Lebailly, Tinne Tuytelaars
arxiv-2410-04959.description: Abstract We present a principled and simplified design of the projector and loss function for non-contrastive self-supervised learning based on hyperdimensional computing. We theoretically demonstrate that this design introduces an inductive bias that encourages representations to be simultaneously decorrelated and clustered, without explicitly enforcing these properties.

arxiv-2501-17549.title: Query-Aware Learnable Graph Pooling Tokens as Prompt for Large Language Models
arxiv-2501-17549.creator: Wooyoung Kim, Byungyoon Park, Wooju Kim
arxiv-2501-17549.description: Abstract Graph-structured data plays a vital role in numerous domains, such as social networks, citation networks, commonsense reasoning graphs and knowledge graphs. While graph neural networks have been employed for graph processing, recent advancements have explored integrating large language models for graph-based tasks.

arxiv-2502-02478.title: Enhanced quantum magnetometry with a laser-written integrated photonic diamond chip
arxiv-2502-02478.creator: Yanzhao Guo, Giulio Coccia, Vinaya Kumar Kavatamane, Argyro N. Giakoumaki, Anton N. Vetlugin, Roberta Ramponi, Cesare Soci, Paul E. Barclay, John P. Hadden, Anthony J. Bennett, Shane M. Eaton
arxiv-2502-02478.description: Abstract An ensemble of negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond can act as a precise quantum sensor even under ambient conditions. In particular, to optimize thier sensitivity, it is crucial to increase the number of spins sampled and maximize their coupling to the detection system, without degrading their spin properties.

arxiv-2602-05124.title: Scalable Fixed-Point Framework for High-Dimensional Hamilton–Jacobi Equations Thanks: Submitted to the editors DATE
arxiv-2602-05124.creator: Yesom Park, Stanley Osher
arxiv-2602-05124.description: Abstract We propose a novel, mesh–free, and gradient–free fixed–point approach for computing viscosity solutions of high-dimensional Hamilton–Jacobi (HJ) equations. By leveraging the Hopf–Lax formula, our approach iteratively solves the associated variational problem via a Picard iteration, enabling efficient evaluation of both the solution and its corresponding control without relying on grids, characteristics, or differentiation.

pmc-10623863.creator: Samuel Ejeta Chibsa, Kenbon Bayisa, Mustefa Adem Hussen, Bilisumamulifna Tefera Kefeni
pmc-10623863.description: BackgroundOver 4.5 million women worldwide have used Implanon. It plays an important role in reducing unwanted conceptions, lowering maternal mortality, and enhancing child survival. As a result, the availability of family planning programmes encourages women to begin using contraception and encourages women who are already using family planning to continue using it.

pmc-11539158.creator: Carlos Dornels Freire de Souza, Rodrigo Feliciano do Carmo

pmc-11544882.title: Enhancing the Nutritional and Bioactive Properties of Bee Pollen: A Comprehensive Review of Processing Techniques
pmc-11544882.creator: María Alcalá-Orozco, Isabella Lobo-Farfan, Diego F Tirado, Diana C Mantilla-Escalante, Olga Escuredo, M Carmen Seijo, María Shantal Rodríguez-Flores
pmc-11544882.description: Bee pollen is recognized as a superfood due to its high content of nutrients and bioactive compounds. However, its bioavailability is restricted by a degradation-resistant outer layer known as exine. Physical and biotechnological techniques have recently been developed to degrade this layer and improve pollen’s nutritional and functional profile.

pmc-12636548.title: Drynachromoside A from Drynaria fortunei attenuates oxidative stress and fibrosis of diabetic nephropathy via activating Nrf2 in vitro and in vivo
pmc-12636548.creator: Huankai Yao, Jindong Li, Ruiqing Wu, Dan Du, Fengwei Ai, Yan Li
pmc-12636548.description: Background:Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is the most common complication of diabetes mellitus. It has shown that the activation of nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) could attenuate DN. To identifiy novel Nrf2 activators targeting DN, we explored drynachromoside A (DCSA) from Drynaria fortunei in vitro and in vivo.

pmc-12683742.title: Nonmass Lesions on Breast Ultrasound: Radiologic-Pathologic Correlation and a Practical Guide to Diagnostic Approach
pmc-12683742.creator: Haejung Kim, Hyunwoo Lee, Ji Soo Choi
pmc-12683742.description: Breast lesions that do not meet the criteria for a mass on ultrasound (US), analogous to asymmetry on mammography or nonmass enhancement on MRI, are frequently encountered during diagnostic or screening US. These lesions, referred to as nonmass lesions (NMLs), are discrete areas of altered echotexture compared to surrounding breast tissue, lacking the threedimensionality or conspicuity of a mass.

pmc-12827328.title: Cortical morphology alterations in non-COVID-19 post-infectious olfactory dysfunction
pmc-12827328.creator: Linyin Yao, Zhifu Sun, Jia Liu, Yichen Guo, Yuying Zang, Xiaoli Yi
pmc-12827328.description: While COVID-19-associated olfactory dysfunction leads to gray matter (GM) structural alterations, it remains unclear whether these structural GM alterations are specific to COVID-19. To address this, we investigated GM changes in patients with post-infectious olfactory dysfunction (PIOD) who tested negative for SARS-CoV-2 infection. This study included 65 patients with PIOD who were SARS-CoV-2 negative and 65 healthy controls.

pmc-13298211.title: Poly(vinyl alcohol) Hydrogels for Osteoarthritis: A Review of Preparation Strategies, Modification Approaches, and Challenges
pmc-13298211.creator: Jiaxuan Di, Yan He, Chao Sun, Jingna Jia, Xing Zheng, Xinyu Li
pmc-13298211.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Articular cartilage has attracted significant attention for its essential roles in joint lubrication and stress buffering. However, its inherent self-repair capacity is limited. Addressing inflammatory damage to this tissue, therefore, presents a major clinical challenge in orthopedics. Poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA)-based hydrogels have emerged as promising repair materials due to their high water content, which mimics the properties of natural cartilage, as well as their tunable mechanical properties and favorable biocompatibility.

pmc-13346787.title: AKR1B1 promotes canine mammary tumorigenesis via activation of PI3K/AKT signaling and acts as a serum biomarker
pmc-13346787.creator: Zhe Cao, Qinyu Zhang, Yujun Zhou, Haoyu Li, Deliang Cao, Zhiliang Sun
pmc-13346787.description: Aldo-keto reductase 1B1 (AKR1B1), also named as aldose reductase, is an enzyme implicated in metabolic regulation and signaling transduction in human cancers, but little is known in canine mammary tumors (CMTs). This study investigated expression in CMT tissues, functional role in tumor progression, and potential of AKR1B1 as a circulating biomarker.

pmc-13457270.title: Gene expression of adipokines in placentas of cows from Northeastern Brazil with and without hyperketonemia and their interactions with metabolic biomarkers
pmc-13457270.creator: Ângela Imperiano da Conceição, João Victor José de Barros Dantas, Carla Lopes de Mendonça, Jobson Filipe de Paula Cajueiro, Rodolfo José Cavalcanti Souto, Licarion Pinto, Daniel Nunes de Araújo Gonçalves, Paulo Roberto Eleutério de Souza, José Augusto Bastos Afonso, Pierre Castro Soares
pmc-13457270.description: The objective was to analyze the mRNA expression of leptin, leptin receptor (ObRb), adiponectin, adiponectin receptor (AdipoR1), and resistin in the placental tissue of cows with and without hyperketonemia, relating it to their metabolic profile. Samples were collected from 135 cows during birth, divided into two groups: G1: without hyperketonemia (n = 120) and G2: with hyperketonemia (n = 15).

pmc-13505087.title: Comparison of compaction techniques for filling isthmuses using Biodentine in mandibular molars
pmc-13505087.creator: Evren Sarıyılmaz, Öznur Sarıyılmaz, Rüya Sessiz, Gülşah Uslu
pmc-13505087.description: BackgroundThis study aimed to compare the filling volume and surface area of Biodentine placed in mandibular molar isthmuses using three different compaction techniques (manual, ultrasonic, and sonic endomotor system).Materials and methodsThirty resin mandibular molars with simulated apical-third isthmuses were randomly assigned to three compaction groups: manual, ultrasonic, and sonic endomotor system.

pmc-13616936.title: More than a free snack: benefits of mobilized resources and socialization for pediatric healthcare workers
pmc-13616936.creator: Thomas B. Ayres, Kristin L. Ray, Aimee M. Hoflander, Angela L. Myers
pmc-13616936.description: IntroductionAddressing the burnout epidemic in the healthcare workforce is a primary concern of the modern healthcare organization and recognized across researchers and leaders of nations. This study aims to test whether a mobilized micro-break intervention, the Wellbeing on Wheels (WOW) Cart, improved health care worker (HCW) energy perceived organizational support and work engagement.
